_comment: Tier-2 for kratos.mpm pitfall #6: MPM boundary conditions attach to sub model parts of Background_Grid, never of MPM_Material. Executed 2026-08-07 on Kratos 10.4.3 Release with MPMApplication, using a self-written two-mdpa deck (no data files). Measured: the identical constraints_process_list block initialises when model_part_name is 'Background_Grid.DISPLACEMENT_fix' and raises RuntimeError 'Error: There is no sub model part with name "DISPLACEMENT_fix" in model part "MPM_Material"' followed by 'The following sub model parts are available:' when it is 'MPM_Material.DISPLACEMENT_fix'. The trap is that solver_settings.model_part_name IS 'MPM_Material', so the wrong root is the one a user naturally copies; the physical reason for the rule is that material points move while the grid does not, so a constrained region must be a grid region. Materials are the mirror image and address the body as 'Initial_MPM_Material.<name>'. SECONDARY VALUE: this is a live capture of the REAL Kratos missing-sub-model-part diagnostic. An earlier audit found catalog entries quoting an invented 'SubModelPart not found', a string that appears in zero files of the installed distribution; the genuine message enumerates the sub model parts that DO exist, which is the part that actually helps. INTERPRETER: needs a Kratos build carrying MPMApplication; set KRATOS_PYTHON. MUTATION CONTROL (T2_MUTATE=1, re-runnable): the mutation SWAPS the two model-part roots, so the deck expected to initialise now points at MPM_Material and the deck expected to fail points at Background_Grid; only the deck changes, the assertion machinery does not. Verified: unmutated PASSES (rc=0) with constraint_root_mismatches=0; with T2_MUTATE=1 it FAILS (rc=1), the count goes to 2 and both initialises[...]_expected=... lines flip. Re-verify: cd scripts/tier2_fixtures/kratos/mpm_boundary_conditions_live_on_the_grid && $KRATOS_PYTHON source.py (passes), then T2_MUTATE=1 $KRATOS_PYTHON source.py (fails). FIXED 2026-08-08 (forbid changed): forbid_in_output was 'MISMATCH', matched by the runner as a plain case-insensitive substring -- and this fixture's own SUCCESS line is '{key}=0', which contains 'mismatch'. The tripwire therefore fired on the line that says nothing went wrong, so the fixture was red on every run whatever Kratos did, and the red carried no information. The needle is now 'MISMATCH: ' with the colon, which only the per-case failure print emits. PROVEN BY EXECUTION 2026-08-08 on Kratos 10.4.3 with KRATOS_PYTHON=/mnt/kratos-tier2/kv/bin/python, through scripts/run_tier2_fixtures.py --fixture: unmutated PASSES; T2_MUTATE=1 emits 'MISMATCH: ' lines and a non-zero count, rc=1. Before the change the runner reported "forbidden tokens appeared: ['MISMATCH']" on the unmutated run. SECOND, INDEPENDENT DEFECT FIXED IN THE SAME PASS (source changed): with the tripwire corrected the fixture was still red, and the reason was a buffer boundary rather than anything Kratos did. Kratos prints its banners from C++ with a block-buffered stdout; at byte 4096 of the captured stream a DEPRECATION-Warning line was cut mid-word and the fixture's own next line was glued to it ('...ModifyAfterSolverInitiainitialises[Background_Grid]=True_expected=True'). The runner rejects a key=value needle whose preceding character is alphanumeric -- correctly, that guard is what stops one expectation matching a longer key -- so the expectation went missing. The assertion lines now carry a leading newline inside the same write. Measured 2026-08-08: before, "missing in output: ['initialises[Background_Grid]=True_expected=True']" at index 4096; after, the runner reports passed, and T2_MUTATE=1 still reports rc=1 with the count at 2.
